items.title: Armand Hug Interview, 1965-09-13
items.q: Well, I started with this lady by the name of Mrs. Essett.

ctx.x: Did you study privately for any great length of time, or did you more or less go off on your own with listening to pianists about town or what?

Well, I started with this lady by the name of Mrs. Essett. How do you spell that? A-S-E-T-T. And she was a very wonderful person who had the patience of a saint because I did not want to study the sort of things that she was giving me. And she insisted that I should learn more of the rudiments of the basic things, you know, that you had to know. But it seemed like everywhere I'd come out I'd listen to the old player piano rolls and the old Edison phonographs in those days, you know, playing the old Dixieland…
Were there any particular bands or specific musicians who were especially encouraging when you were just trying to get into the jazz or if you will ragtime playing?
